solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: My lips melted with his, briefly and naughtily

indicators.note: melted letters run together and set in a new shape, so the pool is rearranged
briefly asks for the word cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A kiss that dissolves lips together, done with a mischievous air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims HIS to HI; 'melted' rearranges MYLIPS with HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a mischievous, puckish way is acting naughtily; the two adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bury is barbarous, and mostly to be shunned

indicators.note: letters to be shunned are kept out, so they are removed from the longer word

parts.note: barbarous means cruel or inhumane

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the last letter of 'and' goes

explanation.surface: A grim remark that burial is savage and best avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts AND to AN; 'to be shunned' takes that AN out of INHUMANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is a formal word meaning to place a body in the ground, to inter it.

clue.text: Bitter denunciation of royal photo

parts.note: Prince Philip was a member of the British royal family
pic is short for picture, a photo

explanation.surface: An angry attack provoked by a picture of a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A philippic, named after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon, is a fierce verbal attack.

clue.text: Impetuous Tottenham player, currently popular?

parts.note: Tottenham Hotspur footballers are known as Spurs, so one is a Spur
something currently popular is fashionable right now, in vogue

explanation.surface: A rash footballer from Tottenham who is the fans' current darling.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club nicknamed Spurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur-of-the-moment act is done on impulse without planning, which is what impetuous means.

clue.text: Washing, initially limp and wet?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words limp and and

parts.note: wet could be described, whimsically, as not dry; the question mark flags the invented word

explanation.surface: Clothes that come out of the machine limp and damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'limp' and 'and'; the question mark admits that UNDRY is a made-up word for wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is clothes and linen that are being or need to be cleaned, the household washing.

clue.text: Hateful hounds eviscerating eland

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs, a dismissive word for hounds

indicators.note: eviscerating removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters of eland

explanation.surface: Vicious dogs disembowelling an antelope on the savannah.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursed can mean detestable or damnable, so it is a synonym of hateful.

clue.text: Punctured by tick, veteran nudist acting cool

indicators.note: a thing punctured by something has that something pushed into it
acting suggests a performance or role, so the letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: a tick and a mo are both short spells of time

explanation.surface: An old naturist, stung by a bloodsucking insect, keeps calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punctured by' puts MO inside the anagram of VETERAN NUDIST that 'acting' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undemonstrative shows little feeling, which is one sense of cool: reserved, unemotional.

clue.text: Scent of animal dropping inhaled by senior

indicators.note: something inhaled by another is taken inside it

parts.note: poo is an animal dropping

explanation.surface: An old person breathing in the smell of animal dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or trail, including the scent, that a wild creature leaves behind.

clue.text: Refuse pile of Spooner's aged weed

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: game meat that is hung is aged before cooking
dill is a herb sold as dill weed

explanation.surface: A heap of rubbish described by the muddled Reverend Spooner as old weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat that is 'hung' has been left to mature, hence aged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunghill is a heap of manure or muck, a pile of refuse.

clue.text: Carpenter's mate was endlessly surly, endlessly rebellious

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of was is cut off
something rebellious is in revolt, so the trimmed word is turned round
the second endlessly cuts the last letter from surly

explanation.surface: A joiner's companion who was grumpy and defiant without end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carpenter is Lewis Carroll's, not a joiner; 'endlessly' works on each of the two words it follows, and 'rebellious' turns only the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' the two characters are companions on the beach.

clue.text: Lofty success announced in 17 syllables

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: lofty is high and a success is a coup, said together as high coup

explanation.surface: A grand triumph declared in a very short poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a Japanese verse form traditionally of seventeen syllables in three lines.

clue.text: Volatile, tailless panda hampered by nasty wound

indicators.note: something hampered by another is hemmed in by it, so it sits inside
nasty suggests the letters are twisted out of shape and rearranged
tailless means the final letter of panda is lost

explanation.surface: A bear without a tail, troubled by an ugly injury and very moody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' makes U DOWN from the injury word, and 'hampered by' sets the trimmed bear between the U and DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up and down is changeable in mood, swinging back and forth, as a volatile person is.

clue.text: Chap reportedly given degree by post

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: a chap is a male
an order is a rank or degree, as in of the first order

explanation.surface: A man said to have got his university qualification through the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail-order goods are bought and delivered through the postal service.

clue.text: Gum sticking hard to back of one's car

indicators.note: the next piece is attached to the back of the earlier ones

parts.note: one's, the speaker's own, is my
RR, Rolls-Royce, stands for a luxury car
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Chewing gum stuck firmly to the rear of someone's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: RR is the Rolls-Royce badge; 'sticking' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrrh is an aromatic resin, a gum oozed by certain trees.

clue.text: Small, daft and pimpled

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing
potty is British slang for daft, silly

explanation.surface: A description of a little, silly, blemished person.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotty face is covered with spots, that is pimpled.

clue.text: Watch predecessor help students from east with Latin

indicators.note: in an across clue, read from east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: aid is help
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: An early timepiece aided by students from the east who know Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'from east' means read right to left; NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Before clocks and watches, people told time by a shadow on a sundial.

clue.text: Dull pair of individuals comprising grandma and husband?

indicators.note: the pair comprises, or contains, the next piece between them

parts.note: I stands for an individual, so a pair is two of the letter
nan is a British word for grandma
a mate is a partner or husband

explanation.surface: A boring couple made up of granny and her other half.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, without spirit, and so dull or sluggish.

clue.text: No doubt you finally get upset, departing

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and rearranged
finally points to the last letter of you

explanation.surface: A consoling remark that you will be distressed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives U, which joins NODOUBT for 'upset' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbound train or flight is one leaving, heading away, so departing.

clue.text: Aunt regularly pursuing her husband, in need of wash

indicators.note: a piece pursuing another follows it, coming after

parts.note: an aunt's husband is an uncle

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of Aunt, the first and third

explanation.surface: An aunt chasing her spouse who badly needs a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean is dirty, so it is in need of a wash.

clue.text: Idiot rocking my punt

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool rocks the boat while punting on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Numpty is Scottish slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A numpty is an informal Scottish word for a foolish person.

clue.text: Rat on fish on punt

indicators.note: on means the fish comes after the punt in an across answer

parts.note: punt is British slang for a bet
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A rodent sitting on a fish lying on a flat boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform against them, a slang synonym for betray.

clue.text: Ken's girlfriend, 1 down, starts to lift large weight in gym

indicators.note: one down means the numeral one, I, has gone down and is dropped

parts.note: Barbie is the doll whose boyfriend is Ken

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letters of lift and large

explanation.surface: Barbie, buried, begins lifting heavy weights in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' looks like a cross-reference to INHUME but means I down, dropped from BARBIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is a long bar with weights at each end, lifted in a gym.

clue.text: Bans cheers and jeers

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British ways to say thanks
boos are jeers

explanation.surface: Forbidding both applause and heckling at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboos are prohibitions, social bans on certain acts or words.

clue.text: Cheer bee on the radio

definitions.meaning: a shout of approval, well done
in the NATO phonetic alphabet used over radio, the letter B is spoken as this word

explanation.surface: A buzzing insect broadcast with a round of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouted at a performance it is a cheer; in radio spelling it stands for the letter B.

clue.text: Befuddled, in the main

definitions.meaning: the main is the open ocean, so this means out on the ocean

explanation.surface: Confused, for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bewildered and literally out on the ocean, the main.

clue.text: Fat girl consuming a cocktail

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the a goes inside

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a cooking fat
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A plump young woman downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a cocktail of tequila, lime and orange liqueur.

clue.text: Get out of sun's heat here

indicators.note: of signals taking the letters out of the following words, which hide them

explanation.surface: Advice to escape the midday sun's heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword or knife is to draw it from its scabbard, to get it out.

clue.text: Perhaps fly adult French pal over and make a move?

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: ami is French for friend
to go is to make a move

explanation.surface: A French friend makes a pass at a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult stage of an insect, a fly being one example.

clue.text: Want expensive filling to be removed from tooth

parts.note: dear means costly, expensive

indicators.note: the filling is the middle letters, which are to be removed, leaving the ends of tooth

explanation.surface: A dentist's pricey filling has to be taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling to be removed from' takes OOT out of TOOTH, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a lack or shortage, which is want in the sense of need.

clue.text: Not all there, unlike this puzzle

definitions.meaning: a crossword is full of hints, so the opposite is a puzzle with none

explanation.surface: Not all there, unlike this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means foolish and witless, and literally without hints, unlike a crossword.
